study: DeCesare et al. 2017 (Retired Mentors for New Teachers mentoring program)
eval_evidence: Independent NCEE/IES evaluation by REL Central (report REL 2017-225); the program was developed by Aurora Public Schools, evaluated by the REL team (separate parties).
developer_evidence: Program developed by Aurora Public Schools; the PD (mentoring) was delivered by recruited retired district educators serving as mentors, not by the program developers or a research team themselves.
cascade_evidence: District-developed mentoring program delivered through an intermediary tier of retired educators recruited and deployed as mentors to the new teachers (developer -> retired mentors -> mentee teachers).
counterfactual_evidence: Control received an active alternative: the district's typical business-as-usual 'buddy' mentoring (~15 hours over the year from a more experienced buddy teacher); the program group got that PLUS the retired mentor.
coaching_evidence: Mentees met weekly one-on-one with their mentor and monthly in the classroom; mentors used classroom observation and feedback, modeling, co-teaching, and lesson design/delivery support — recurring in-class coaching in the teacher's own classroom.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention is teacher mentoring/coaching of new teachers; only the teacher's instruction is affected, no direct student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-year intervention (2013/14 + 2014/15); end-of-treatment student outcomes (the primary records) measured at end of Year 2, after a prior implementation year. (Year-1 wave reported separately as interim, and was the only significant math result.)
